target_name: Fixed charges against internal resources with maturing debt
rationale: Swapping the realized repayment flow (dltr) for the forward-looking stock of debt due within a year is an economically substantive, coverage-improving change to the archive's best-alpha construct, though the resulting signal is close to a short-term-leverage-minus-cash/cash-flow composite whose legs are individually well-documented anomalies, so any alpha will need attribution against leverage and cash-holdings controls.

Industry demeaning of the exact archive expression is a low-novelty, standard neutralization rather than a new mechanism, but the utility/regulated-payout argument is a coherent diagnosis of why the linear cross-sectional slope was flat while the decile spread was strong, so it is a defensible (if incremental) test.

This is mechanical three-year smoothing of an existing signal (ranking a TS_SUM is monotone-equivalent to ranking the mean), and the resource leg is internally incoherent because it cumulates a stock (che) across years alongside a flow (oancf), triple-counting the same cash balance rather than measuring cumulative resources.

The stated economics are explicitly conditional ("survivable in a growing business... compounds in a contracting one") but SUMRANK implements a compensatory sum in which extreme dilution-free strain or pure revenue contraction alone can dominate, and the sales-contraction leg has already shown a sign-contradicting FMB slope in the archive, so a strong alpha would most likely be inherited from the strain leg.

Varying only the resource leg is a genuinely informative ablation of the one untested design choice in the archive's strongest portfolio result, though wcap subsumes che and largely restates the current-ratio conditioners already explored, so the expected incremental information is modest.

target_name: Fixed-charge strain met by fresh equity
rationale: The mechanism (how the strain is funded) is the most interesting in the batch, but the hypothesis is explicitly conjunctive — strain *and* simultaneous share creation — while SUMRANK is additive and will assign top scores to heavy diluters with no strain and to strained firms issuing nothing, so MIN or a product is the operator the stated economics require.
